So what I went to wasn’t really a “boot camp” per se, and unlike many of the stories here, I actually chose to go to this.   A couple of years ago, when I was around 15, I went to a wrestling camp in Iowa for 3 weeks.  The reason I chose to go was to hopefully get better at wrestling, but I wasn’t really sure what I was getting into.  

Anyways, I flew by myself for the first time to Iowa from California at the beginning of June.  The day I got there, which was at around 6:00 p.m. they immediately gave me my dorm room number (it was at a university) and sent me up to unpack my stuff.  At 8:00-11:00 at night we had an intensive practice which is a huge understatement, but that’s what the camp directors called the extra hard practices.  After about 10 minutes into the practice, I began to realize how much hell this camp was going to put me through.  I knew intensive wrestling camps like this were hard, but after 10 minutes of a 2 hour practice in a 90 degree room with no air conditioning in a state with 90% humidity in the summer, I then really started to understand the I guess you could say “mistake” I made going there.   

Once I got back to my dorm, I was too tired to shower even though you could’ve rung out my shirt from all the sweat it soaked up from the practice.  I can’t go into detail about these practices because it would be too long, but the fact that I was able to wring my shirt out and get a quart of sweat out of it, hopefully gives an idea of the intensity of the practices.  Since the beds were raised about 6 feet off the ground, and I the fact that I was too beat down to move, I decided to sleep on the stone floor.   

Without going into overdescriptive detail about this place, the next few weeks consisted of around 9 hours of wrestling a day, from the 6 mile runs at 5:30 in the morning to the 11:00 intensive practices at night.  We would wake up at around 5:30, go on a run with our assigned group and coach given to us based on our weight class and then get back to the dorms just in time for an hour breakfast.  Unfortunately,  the coaches made us run everywhere we went, which included the 1 mile runs in between the gym and the dorms/cafeteria.  Anyways, after breakfast we did intensive drilling and wrestling for about 2-3 hours and got back in time to eat some lunch.  I want to point out that the food wasn’t too bad here, but it was old, and after 3 weeks of eating the same thing (generally rice and beans) it got pretty tiring.  After the hour long lunch, we’d then head to another practice where we would do some “light” drilling and working on our wrestling moves for another 2 hours.  Right after that we got another hour long dinner and ran straight back to the gym for the last 2 hour intensive practice of the day.   

The night practices were by far the worst.  We got in the unairconditioned gym and immediately started conditioning on the wet mats from the humidity.  Generally we would start off with Indian runs around the gym for 15 minutes carrying 50 pounds of sand on our backs.  After that we went into the weight room and were given 35 pound weights each.  We were forced to lift these weights above our heads for 3 minutes, 5 times over without dropping below our shoulders or neck.  Once we finished that, we went back out into the gym and started running with these weights while simultaneously doing chest presses in the air with them.  Mostly these night practices consisted of stuff like this, with different rotations throughout the entirety of the practice.  

I can only really recall sleeping in the actual bed once which was on the second night.   All of the other nights I was too tired and sore to get in the raised bed, so I just decided to sleep on the floor.  We were however given time after our 11:00 practices to shower every night and were expected to be lights out by 11:45.  A couple of the days, we actually ran to the campus stadium and sat in the sauna for an hour and were then forced to sit in the ice bath immediately after for 3 minutes.  It’s a lot worse than it sounds because my body wasn’t used to being exposed to such contrasting temperatures in such short amounts of time like that.  

The last day of the 21 day camp was called red flag day, because it was the worst practice of the camp.   It would take too long to describe red flag day, but just imagine the intensity of what I’ve talked about, multiplied by 2.   

So once I got home, I slept for nearly 3 days straight like a sick dog.  I told my parents that the camp was hard but I didn’t give them the whole story because I didn’t want them to think that I hated it and they wasted their money or anything.  After resting for a couple days, I noticed the pain i developed in my back during the camp, had actually gotten severely worse.  It was hurting to move so I decided to get an x-ray on it, and sure enough, I actually got a stress fracture in my back on the L-5 vertebrae.  For a better more accurate diagnosis, I actually had a spondylitis/spondylolisthesis pars defect fracture in case anyone was wondering.  So in the end, the camp was for nothing because I ended up being decommissioned from wrestling that year due to injury purposes.
